name: saturday-race
description: Ground truth for the first real race captured with the app — Saturday 15 August 2026 on the Waitematā, course "13 - 15/08". `saturday-race.log` beside this file is the plotter's bytes exactly as the capture recorder wrote them: a B&G Zeus 3 stream with no `\c:` tag block, so replay timing comes from the GPS clock (see `rawLogReplay.ts`). `marks` is the linked course in sailed order, transcribed from the dev app's `courseMark`/`mark` rows — `id` is the `courseMark` row id, which is what `detectSailedLegs` reports as `courseMarkId`. A course of 8 marks is a race of 7 legs; the review pipeline reported 4, which is what this fixture exists to diagnose (tickets 21 and 22).
truthSource: Derived from the log itself for ticket 21: every fix's distance to every course mark, taking each mark's nearest pass. The eight passes fall in course order with no ambiguity — 7-143 m at the marks, versus 190 m or worse for any other near pass — so `roundings` is the sailed truth and `sailedLegs` is that truth as legs. Two decoy passes are what a naive detector trips on: Resolution again at 191 m (00:49:16Z, still manoeuvring before the start proper) and North Head at 153 m (02:10:15Z) while running down the Salt Works to Orakei leg.
viaPointNote: Confirmed by Logan 18 August 2026: courseMark 7 (the FIRST North Head) was not a race mark. It is a via point, entered so the course routes around the North Head peninsula on the way to Salt Works; the boat passed it at 143 m because the headland forces that line, not because it rounded a buoy. courseMark 9 (the second North Head) is the actual race buoy. So this course is 7 legs as entered and 6 legs as raced — Resolution to Salt Works is one race leg, split in two by the via point. The course model cannot yet tell the two apart (a via-points / additional-marks feature is in progress on another branch); until it can, detection should anchor on all 8 entries, which files the data correctly and splits one race leg in two rather than merging two into one.
